solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Had a plan of note — relief all round

indicators.note: says the word for relief encloses the note on every side

parts.note: relief in the sense of help or assistance is aid
me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone with a musical scheme is relieved when it comes off all round.
explanation.definitionFit: To have aimed at something is to have intended or planned it, so the past-tense verbs match.

clue.text: Absolutely everyone in a lake gets wet, presumably

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
to land something is to get or secure it
wet would presumably be the opposite of dry, playfully written as un-dry

explanation.surface: Everyone who goes into a lake will, one assumes, get soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: UNDRY is an invented word, hence the question-mark-like 'presumably'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means every single person, without exception.

clue.text: Country, say, America, then India, toured by host

indicators.note: touring around means going round, so the host's letters surround the others

parts.note: an MC, master of ceremonies, hosts an event
US is the United States
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A host tours a country, America, then India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like a nation, but with 'say' it is an example: country and western.
explanation.definitionFit: Country is a genre, an example of the art of sound and song.

clue.text: Ideal combination of art made me excited

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says art has thrilled them into a perfect pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of the best possible members, a perfect line-up of people.

clue.text: Ties with the Republicans are flourishing

parts.note: the GOP, the Grand Old Party, is the US Republican Party
to tie shoes is to lace them, so ties are laces

explanation.surface: Neckties worn by Republican politicians are apparently all the rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes places is succeeding and prospering, an idiom for flourishing in life or career.

clue.text: Turned up large stake used in wooden structure

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: large means big
a stake is a wager, a bet

explanation.surface: A large wooden post is driven into a frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stake' looks like a wooden post, fitting the surface, but is a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallows-like frame from which executed criminals were hung, built of timber.

clue.text: Beer and punch bottles answer artist's requirement?

indicators.note: to bottle is to contain, so the beer word holds the letter

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer
to box is to punch

explanation.surface: A painter needs beer and punch in bottles, the clue jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter needs a case of colours, the kit an artist carries.

clue.text: Papers turned up in car, briefly — and so do books?

indicators.note: places the turned papers inside the shortened car
cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Someone finds their papers in the car, and wonders if books do too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like 'found' but reverses ID to DI; 'briefly' drops the last O of AUTO.
explanation.definitionFit: To do the books is to inspect a firm's accounts, the job of an accountant checking them.

clue.text: Making one count, perhaps, in French: nothing flashy!

parts.note: en is French for in
no means none, nothing
bling is showy jewellery, flashy display

explanation.surface: Someone says, in French, that there is nothing showy about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like the verb, but it is the nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising someone to the peerage, for example as a count, is to make them noble.

clue.text: Free from outside interference, one's on a roll?

definitions.text: Free from outside interference, one's on a roll?

parts.words: Free from outside interference, one's on a roll?
parts.note: a protected structure may not have its exterior altered, and it appears on an official roll, the statutory register of buildings of special interest

explanation.surface: Someone left to their own devices is enjoying a winning streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On a roll' looks like the idiom for a run of success but means entered on a list. In Britain, specially protected historic structures are entered on a statutory list and cannot be changed without permission.
explanation.definitionFit: A protected historic structure is shielded from alteration and recorded on the national register, which is the roll.

clue.text: Section of course where champions feature in commentary?

parts.note: to champion is to support or back, so champions are backs

indicators.note: commentary is spoken, so a word said aloud gives the letters

parts.note: a feature is a characteristic, a trait

explanation.surface: A racecourse commentator describes where the favourites show up.
explanation.walkthrough: BACKS, then 'trait' as some say it, with the T sounded, giving TRAIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: On a racetrack, the straight stretch opposite the finish is part of the track.

clue.text: Unhappily married twice, not once, I've nothing to say!

indicators.note: unhappily suggests things are out of sorts, so the letters are rearranged
the abbreviation for married is used two times

explanation.surface: A twice-wed person, unhappy both times, refuses to discuss it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unhappily' shuffles MM (married, twice) with the letters of NOT ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock reply of someone declining to answer questions, used as an exclamation.

clue.text: Bone's top section facing the wrong way

indicators.note: says the letters are turned to read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or top, written here as AI
a section is a bit

explanation.surface: The upper part of a skeleton's bone has been put in back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facing the wrong way' turns AIBIT around. A1 (top quality) is written AI, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The shinbone of the lower leg, one of the long bones of the skeleton.

clue.text: Not all the members having payment ready

parts.note: a sub is a subscription payment, as for club membership
ready to go, as in 'all set'

explanation.surface: Only some of a club's members have their subscriptions ready to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: In set theory a portion of a group's elements is a subset, so not every member is included.

clue.text: Farm, old, nevertheless is about to diversify

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for nevertheless goes around

parts.note: but means nevertheless
a ranch is a farm

explanation.surface: An old farm is nevertheless about to diversify its business.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand into new areas of activity, as a tree spreads limbs.

clue.text: Fawn's hoof — and light coat?

parts.note: to hoof a ball is to kick it hard, to boot it
a lick of paint is a thin coat

explanation.surface: A young deer's foot and its pale coat are described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fawn' looks like the young deer, but it is the verb: to grovel or flatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To fawn is to flatter servilely, the same sense as the verb to toady to someone.

clue.text: Long battle sailor has to keep girl in line

indicators.note: keeping something is holding it, so the sailor's letters surround the rest

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: places the girl inside the line

parts.note: a row is a line
Jan is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A sailor struggles for ages to keep his girlfriend in check.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary siege of Troy lasted ten years, a famously lengthy conflict.

clue.text: They're using key copies to get outside jailhouse finally?

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

indicators.note: the copying word goes round the outside of the letter

parts.note: to ape is to copy

indicators.note: takes the last letter of jailhouse

explanation.surface: Prisoners use duplicated keys to break out of jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue paints the scene of a breakout, with 'They're' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who have broken out of prison, the people the pronoun refers to.

clue.text: Seminars replaced meeting thankfully avoided

indicators.note: the letters are put back in different places, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seminars were swapped for something else, so a dreaded meeting never happened.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape from a collision is a close call, an encounter that just failed to happen.

clue.text: The truth one's revolted against, finally searched for

parts.note: 'it is so' means it is true, so so stands for the truth
ugh is what someone disgusted says

indicators.note: takes the last letter of against

explanation.surface: Someone finally sought out the truth after rebelling against it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolted' looks like rebellion but means disgusted, giving the exclamation UGH.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of seek, meaning looked for or pursued.

clue.text: Waste of wine: scandal

parts.note: red is red wine
mud is dirt or scandal, as in mudslinging

explanation.surface: A scandal over a waste of good wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The caustic residue left over from refining bauxite into alumina, an industrial by-product.

clue.text: Narrative that's mostly urban?

indicators.note: all but the end is kept, so the final letter goes

parts.note: urban means relating to a town or city, so re city (concerning city)

explanation.surface: A story asks whether it is largely set in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Urban means 'relating to a city', read as RE (about) + CITY; 'mostly' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A récit is a French-derived word for a story or account, especially the narrative portion of a book.

clue.text: Symbol of bear on bottom of form

parts.note: to bear is to carry, to tote

indicators.note: in a down clue, the bottom letter is the last letter

explanation.surface: A symbol of a bear appears at the foot of a form.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem, often an animal, revered as a sign of a clan or group.

clue.text: Porter cross with artist portraying Queen

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
X is the shape of a cross
and means together with
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An irritable doorman and a painter work on a royal portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a doorman but is the beer. Alexandra was queen consort to Edward VII.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandra of Denmark was a British queen consort, wife of King Edward VII.

clue.text: Large church found by couple on way to work

parts.note: a duo is a pair
MO is modus operandi, a method of working

explanation.surface: A couple discover a big church on their commute.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian term for a cathedral, the principal church of a city.

clue.text: Plea for understanding from modern wife got gent flustered

indicators.note: being flustered means thrown into confusion, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A contemporary wife has rattled a gentleman, who begs not to be misunderstood.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase asking a listener not to misinterpret what is about to be said, a request to be understood.

clue.text: What mister did to maiden is covered by a pressman

indicators.note: says the inner letters sit wrapped inside the outer ones

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a newspaperman
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A journalist hushes up what a gentleman did to a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister' looks like Mr, a man, but is a spray device that turns liquid into a fine mist.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray bottle reduces liquid to tiny droplets, which is what atomising means.

clue.text: Sleep, as bird does, with sailor in bunk

indicators.note: places the sailor inside the word for nonsense

parts.note: bunk is nonsense, rot
OS is an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor in his bunk sleeps like a perched bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' looks like a ship's bed but means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds settle on a perch to rest for the night, and that verb is to roost.
